questions.solution:
The correct answer is: b

∵ Winner gets 80% of polled votes

Difference between them = 60% = 600

Total number of polled votes = 1000
Half of total number of votes polled = 1000/2 = 500

questions.question: In this question, a statement is followed by two arguments numbered I and II. Based on the statement, you have to decide which of the arguments is strong. Statement: Should there be reservation in Government jobs for candidates from single child family? Arguments: I. No. This is not advisable as the jobs should be offered to only deserving candidates without any reservation for a particular group. II. Yes. This will help reduce the growing population in India as the parents will be encouraged to adopt single child soon.
questions.questionHtml:
In this question, a statement is followed by two arguments numbered I and II. Based on the statement, you have to decide which of the arguments is strong.

Statement: Should there be reservation in Government jobs for candidates from single child family?

Arguments:

I. No. This is not advisable as the jobs should be offered to only deserving candidates without any reservation for a particular group.

II. Yes. This will help reduce the growing population in India as the parents will be encouraged to adopt single child soon.
questions.solution:
The correct option is: c

The Government has already made provisions for reservation of jobs for the economically backward sections, which is must. So, abolishing the practice of reservation altogether has no meaning. Thus, argument I is vague. Also, more reservations would lead to non-recruitment of many more deserving candidates. Besides, such a reservation, if implemented, will cater to the job requirements of only small section of population and not a major part of it. So, argument II also does not hold strong.
